implementation_notes: Ruby's `Enumerable` usually erases the third copy: three loops over collections become one method taking a block. Extract a module only when three classes share a real responsibility, not merely three similar loops.
idiom_name: Enumerable + block replaces the third copy
code_sketch:
def index_by(records) = records.each_with_object({}) { |r, acc| acc[r.key] = r }
# rather than three near-identical index-building loops
pitfalls: Concern extracted at the second includer
Case/when duplicated across three methods instead of one
